findings.claim: OAuth state is pipeline.signature, a constant md5 of view class names identical for every user/session, so the state check at :412 provides no CSRF protection; an attacker can forge the setup callback (code + state, and installation_id which OAuthLoginView binds from request.GET) into a victim's in-progress pipeline, binding the attacker's GitHub login so the new user-match check passes.
findings.evidence: pipeline/base.py:132-133 computes signature as md5_text of view FQNs; tests hardcode state=9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3 across different users/orgs; ponytail seat reproduced that value with a python md5 one-liner; identity/oauth2.py:245-252,318-325 uses secrets.token_hex() bound to pipeline state. Exploit path reasoned, not run.
findings.reason: Three seats independently; constant value confirmed by command. Fix: random state bound via bind_state and compared to fetch_state (or reuse OAuth2LoginView).

findings.claim: integration.metadata['sender']['login'] raises KeyError (HTTP 500) when the Integration has no 'sender' metadata, which is the normal state for pipeline-created or pre-existing integrations on the reinstall path (Integration exists, OrganizationIntegration does not).
findings.evidence: build_integration writes sender only if state.get('sender') (integration.py:376-377); webhook.py:202-209 is the only writer; ensure_integration (integration pipeline.py:38-42) overwrites metadata; test_integration.py:302-308 asserts pipeline-created integration lacks sender; installation.py:44 guards 'sender' not in metadata. Existing reinstall test deletes Integration too so never hits this branch. Reasoned, not run.
findings.reason: Three seats with source citations. Red test: create Integration without sender and no OrganizationIntegration, run init + setup with valid state, expect error page not KeyError.

findings.claim: The authenticated-user == installer check is skipped entirely when no Integration row exists yet (except Integration.DoesNotExist -> next_step()); build_integration then resolves any installation_id via the app JWT, so anyone knowing an installation id can claim it into their org until the installation webhook is processed.
findings.evidence: integration.py:481 path has no github_authenticated_user comparison; Integration row is created by installation webhook (webhook.py:200-209), which can be delayed or race the user redirect. Reasoned.
findings.reason: Correctness seats agree on the gap (superpowers Important, OCR Minor); no evidence to reject. Normalised to Important since it leaves the patch's stated security goal open in the race window.

findings.claim: test_installation_not_found now passes for the wrong reason: it sends state=ddd023d87a913d5226e2a882c4c4cc05 (not the pipeline signature), so OAuthLoginView rejects at the state check before build_integration runs; the 404 stub is never hit and the 'installation could not be found' path is untested.
findings.evidence: test_integration.py:392 uses ddd023d8...; other tests use 9cae5e88...; integration.py:412-413 returns error() on state mismatch; assertion changed from b'The GitHub installation could not be found.' to generic b'Invalid installation request.'. Reasoned.
findings.reason: Two seats; test no longer guards the behaviour it is named for.

findings.claim: Token-exchange/user-fetch failures are mishandled: safe_urlopen and get_user_info (raise_for_status) are outside the try, so network errors or GitHub 4xx/5xx give a 500 instead of the error page; meanwhile the broad except Exception around safe_urlread/parse silently swallows errors with no logging.
findings.evidence: integration.py:423 safe_urlopen outside try; :428 except Exception: payload = {}; :434 get_user_info -> identity/github/provider.py:16 resp.raise_for_status(); oauth2.py logs SSL/connection/decode errors separately. Reasoned.
findings.reason: Small, contained; route failures to error() and log.

findings.claim: Authorize URL built by f-string without URL-encoding client_id, state, redirect_uri.
findings.evidence: integration.py:408 f-string; identity/oauth2.py:250 uses urlencode(params); works today only because setup URL contains no &, ?, #.
findings.reason: Trivial switch to urlencode; test asserting raw form must be updated.

findings.claim: error() calls _(error_short) on a variable while call sites now pass plain literals, so makemessages no longer extracts these strings and existing translations will drop on the next catalog rebuild.
findings.evidence: integration.py:141; previously _('GitHub installation pending deletion.') etc.; strings exist in src/sentry/locale catalogs; Makefile:61 makemessages workflow.
findings.reason: Wrap literals in _() at call sites, drop _() inside error().

findings.claim: Integration is fetched twice with inconsistent filters (first at :478 without status, second at :494 with status=ACTIVE): an extra query, and a non-active Integration without OrganizationIntegration now gets the generic error where it previously proceeded to next_step/ensure_integration.
findings.evidence: integration.py:478 Integration.objects.get(external_id=...) result discarded; :494 re-fetch with status=ObjectStatus.ACTIVE.
findings.reason: Reuse first result; decide intended behaviour for non-active rows explicitly.

findings.claim: Identity check compares mutable GitHub login strings instead of stable user id; a user who renamed their account between install and link is wrongly rejected.
findings.evidence: webhook.py:205 stores sender.id; get_user_info returns id.
findings.reason: Single seat but cited; low-cost change folded into the KeyError fix at the same line.

findings.claim: OAuthLoginView hand-rolls an OAuth2 flow that already exists (OAuth2LoginView/OAuth2CallbackView via NestedPipelineView + IdentityProviderPipeline with the registered 'github' identity provider, as Slack and VSTS do); the copy lost the random state, urlencode and error logging.
findings.evidence: identity/oauth2.py:210-357; slack/integration.py:126 and vsts/integration.py:433 use NestedPipelineView; identity/github/provider.py registers 'github'; code comments say 'similar to OAuth2CallbackView'. Seat raised as Critical; normalised to Important because the security consequences are tracked separately (state, error handling, encoding).
findings.reason: ponytail: advisory over-engineering; replacement is reasoned not run and depends on the GitHub app callback URL accepting the nested identity pipeline redirect. Fixing the state/encoding/error findings in place resolves the risk; revisit reuse separately.

findings.claim: The setup_path + urlencode({code, state=<md5>}) block is copy-pasted six times with the magic state hash hardcoded each time.
findings.reason: ponytail: advisory test duplication; becomes mandatory cleanup when the state fix makes state random.
